Technical Specifications-OPAL

Termite Control. Treatment
1.

SCOPE

1.1.

The scope of work for anti termite treatment includes injection of insecticide in
sides and bottom of foundation trenches, spraying on stockpiled backfill material
and injections of the insecticide in floor sub-grade of the building. The scope also
covers treatment of all wood works with insecticides before installation in
position, or any activity that in the Opinion of the Engineer is required.

2.

SUBMITTALS

2.1.

All the Material for this activity shall be provided by the Client. The Contractor
shalt Submit Methodology that shall state how the activity shall be executed.

2.2.

The Contactor shall prepare the surface for execution and shall acquire written
approval from the Engineer for the work to be commenced.

2.3.

The Contactor shall submit submittal for the inspection to the Engineer of said
activity once it is completed.

3.

Reference

ASTM D3345 - 17 Standard Test Method for Laboratory Evaluation of Solid Wood
for Resistance to Termites
UFGS 3131 16.19 - TERMITE CONTROL BARRIERS

4.

QUALITY ASSURANCE

4.1. In addition to the requirements of these specifications, the manufacturer's
instructions and recommendations for the work, including preparation of
substrata and application shall be complied with Engineer Instructions for the
execution of this activity.

5.

Application

5.1.

A professional operator shall be engaged who shall have license in accordanc
regulations of governing authorities for application of soil treatment sot
shall be replaced in the opinion of the Engineer.

Technical Specifications-OPAL

6.

MATERIAL

6.1.

An emulsible concentrated insecticide shall be used for dilution with water,
specially formulated to prevent infestation by termites. Fuel oil will not be
permitted as a diluent. Provide a working solution for chemicals with clean
portable water in ratio directed by the engineer that shall comply with
manufacturer's instructions unless other wise specified by the manufacturer!
supplier.

7.

Preparations / Mixing

7.1.

All mixing shall be done at site and mixing proportion of insecticide with water
shall be verified by Engineer.

7.2.

Pure turpentine shall be used for dilution of insecticide, in approved proportion for
application to woodwork where such application is required.

8.

METHOD AND EXTENT OF APPLICATION

8.1.

Insecticide solution shall be applied with approved pressure spraying equipment
maintaining a pressure of 150 PSI to all applications to, on or in earth.

8.2.

Soil treatment shall begin after all work of preparation of earth prior to
installation of concrete has been done. After application, no additional earth
moving or work upon sub grade will be allowed, unless directed by the Engineer.

8.3.

No covering of earth or concrete should be applied over soil treatment until at
least 24 hours after treatment has been made. Solution should not be applied
during wet weather, or when the earth surface is excessively wet.

8.4.

Application should be made to all areas beneath concrete stabs-on-grade,
including sidewalks and paving abutting buildings for distance of at least 2 meters
beyond building line.

8.5.

Solution shall be applied as specified by the Manufacturer and/or as directed by
the Engineer.

Technical Specifications-OPAL

8.6.

Insecticide shall penetrate to a depth of 25-mm minimum in porous earth at
bottom and 50 mm to 75 mm at sides of excavations.

8.7.

Sides of foundation excavations, grade beam, and similar areas shall, be treated
with solution as specified by the Manufacturer, and at all locations where concrete
slabs for platforms and similar work abut the building.

8.8.

Similar treatment shalt be made at all locations where expansion joints, control
joints, column bases and similar work occur at or below grade slabs.

8.9.

In the areas of application signs shall be fixed to show that soil treatment has been
applied. Such signs shall be removed when areas are covered by other
construction.

8.10. Care shall be exercised to ensure that no marks or damage occurs to the finished
structure as a result of the work under this section.
**All woodwork for the entire project is to be
insecticide treated (before application of
Solution). Insecticide shall be sprayed on aLL
surfaces of all the wooden work viz., door
frames, blocking, furring, planks, boards etc.
before installation. Spraying is to be done at
the site, after delivery and before installation.
No spraying shall be necessary after field
sawing jointing or installation of such
material.

9.1.

The cost there of shall be deemed to have been included in the quoted unit rate of
the respective items of the Tender for the activity and the pre-requisites required
that are, but not limited to
i.

Termite control treatment on wood works.

ii.

Turpentine & Water required for mixing insecticide solution.

iii.

Transportation of material and storage at site.

iv.

Anti-termite treatment on stock piled backfill material.

v.

Tool, plant & equipment required for Termite control treatme

FILL and BackfiLL and De-Watering

1.

SCOPE OF WORK;

1.1.

The work covered under this section of specification consists of furnishing all
plant, Labor, equipment, appliances and materials and in performing all operation
in connection with dewatering filling and back filling for all construction works,
complete in strict accordance with the section of the specifications/Direction of
the Engineer, the applicable drawings and subject to terms and conditions of the
contract.

1.2.

The contractor shall inspect the site and acquaint himself fully and completely
with all varyingsoit conditions before commencement of this activity.

2.

RELATED SECTIONS

3.

Drainage of site and protection from storm water inflow:

3.1.

The contractor will be responsible to keep the Site in dry state. He will be checking
the inflow of rain water from outside of the site and will pump out any rain water,
subsoil water, storm water, leakage from sewers or water supply mains or any
waste water ad shall keep the site neat and clean.

3.2.

The contractor shall have included the amount in his quoted amount for the
section of this work.

3.3.

The contractor shall control the grading in the vicinity of the site of the
order to prevent any water from moving into the excavated areas.

4.

Protection of Existing Building, works and under construction structure

Technical Specifications-OPAL
4.1.

The contractor shall provide at his own cost all requisite, needling a strengthening
or other support to retaining walls, floors, etc., necessary for holding in position
and safety of existing hailing, adjoining structures, embankments and ground, and
the basement structure and to protect the adjoining Client s and the general
public. The contactor shall at his cost alter, adopt and maintain all such temporary
works as may be necessary from time to time and finally clear away and make
good all disturbed items. He will make necessary provisions in his Contractor rates
for excavation to the extent to cover his liabilities adequately without any extra
claims or any extra payment on this account. The contactor will be held solely
responsible for the safety of the under-construction structure and adjoining
structure against sliding of earth, and the stability of adjoining ground and
buildings.

5.

Protection of Utility Lines

5.1.

When any existing utility tines whether to be retained or to be removed are
encountered within the areas of operations the contractor shalt notify the
Engineer and shall not proceed until necessary measures are taken for protection
or removal of the lines and instructions are obtained from the engineer. This will
be done at no extra cost to the employer.

5.2.

Excess and undesirable materials, from excavation, not required for fill or back fill
shall be disposed, removed and or deposited and leveled on the site where directed
by the Engineer. Earth suitable and meant for backfill shall be stored at site or at
locations approved by the Engineer in a manner not to interfere with the progress
of construction works at no extra cost.

6.

FILLAND BACK FILL:

Technical Specifications-OPAL

6.1.

No return filling shall be done until, the entire foundations and footings etc., have
been inspected, approved and measured by the Engineer.

6.2.

Where concrete slabs are to be placed on porous fill, any barns, organic and other
unsuitable material shall be removed. Fill, where required to raise the sub - grade
for concrete slabs, shall be clean earth unadulterated sand and gravel and shall be
free of wood, shrubs and other debris. Excavated materials shall be used for fill or
backfill if approved by the Engineer. Fill shall be compacted by a power roller or
other approved equipment, in layers not more than 150 mm (6") thick. Each layer
shall be uniformly spread, moistened and then compacted up to 95% modified
ASSHTO-T 180 density.

6.3.

After completion of foundation footings, walls, slabs, and other construction
below the elevation of the final grades and prior to back filling, forms shall be
removed and excavation shall be cleaned of trash and debris. No back filling shall
be done until the entire foundation and footings have been cured, inspected,
approved and measured by the Engineer. Back fill shall be placed in horizontal
layers not more than 150 mm (6") thick and shall have a proper moisture content
for the required degree of compactions of 95%. Each layer shall be compacted by
mechanical tampers or by other suitable equipment approved by the Engineer.
Back fill shall be brought to a suitable elevation above grades to provide for
anticipated settlement and shrinkage thereof.

6.4.

Back fill shall be placed against foundation walls etc., prior to approve by the
Engineer. Back fill shall be brought up evenly on each side of walls as far as
practicable. Heavy equipment for spreading and compacting back fill shall not be
operated closer to the walls than a distance equal to the height of the back fill
above the top of footing.

7.

COMPACTION - ASTM D698

7.1.

Fill add/or back fill within the building or structures and for a distance of 1.5
meters (5 feet) outside structure shall be compacted to the densities called for
below.

7.2.

The required density of compaction shall be 95 - 100 % of maximum mo
AASHTO density at optimum moisture content under concrete slabs and i

Technical Specifications-OPAL

locations shalt be 95% of maximum modified AASHTO density at optimum
moisture content under concrete slabs and in other Locations shall be 95% of
maximum modified ASSHTO density at optimum moisture content.

8.

ROUGH GRADING:

9.

Necessary rough grading shall be carried out by the contractor to establish the
finished grade or construction requirements of the site. Grades not otherwise
indicated shall be inform levels or stopes between points and existing finished
grades. Abrupt changes in slopes shall be rounded. Additional fill required to
complete rough grading shall be provided as directed by the Engineer.

9.1.

Where paving or slabs are specified, all rough grading shall be done to the sub —
grade of the base course, removing alt targe stones and debris and shalt be
compacted informally to the correct lines and levels ready to receive the paving or
slab. Refilling where required shall be from be excavation with suitable selected
materials in layers not exceeding 150 mm (6") thick and thoroughly compacted, to
the required density.

10.

FOOTING BOIFOM ELEVATIONS;

10.1. The elevations are noted in the drawings are only approximate to and must be
adjusted in the field depending on the soil condition encountered. No concrete
shall begin until the soil bearing capacity test is submitted by visual inspection by
the Engineer. The contractor in planning his work shall make arrangements and
provisions to construct the lowest level footing first.

11.

DISPOSAL OF SURPLUS EARTH SPOIL;

11.1.

All surplus earth and spoil shall be disposed of from the site as directed by the
Engineer. The terms disposal shall include all operation of loading, unloading
stacking, spreading, re — handling, filling depressions, leveling and grad in:
instruction of the Engineer with no — extra cost to employer.

9.6.

positions as shown on the drawings and shall be securely wired or fixed in such
position (both vertically and laterally) while the concrete is being placed and is
setting. Care shall also be taken that the cover to the reinforcement is correctly
adhered to and support bars, spacers and steel chairs, in accordance with the
placing instructions outlined in the C.R.S.I reinforcing steel placing hand book,
shall be provided by the contractor and secured to the reinforcement in such a
manner that the requisite cover is obtained and not altered. Each intersection of
bars shall be adequately tied with No.16 SWG annealed iron or by other approved
means. The contractor shall in the rates for reinforcement and the necessary
typing wire chairs and spacers.

REINFORCEMENT

SCOPE

The work under this section of specifications consists of Cutting, fabricating,
bending, Transporting, Storing and placing steel reinforcement and Welded wire
fabric in concrete structures or elsewhere as shown on the drawings or as directed
by Engineer. The scope of this section of specification is covered with detailed
specifications as laid down herein.

4.

MATERIAL AND SIZE OF BARS

4.1.

Reinforcement for concrete shall conform to the respective Pakistan, British,
ASTM, or other Standards as specified in the Drawings and in the Contract
Documents or as may be specified by Engineer.

4.2.

Unless otherwise specified, all reinforcing bars shall comply with the requirements
of ASTM-A 615 Deformed Billet steel bars and shall have a minimum yield strength
of 40,000 Psi.

4.3.

Unless otherwise specified, all grade 60 reinforcing bars shall comply with the
requirements of ASTM-A 615M for Deformed steel bars and shall have a minimum
yield strength of 60,000 Psi.

4.4. Steel wire mesh reinforcement shall conform to requirements of ASTM
Designation A 185-64 or BS. 4482 and 4483, Standard Specifications for Welded

Steel Wire Fabric for concrete reinforcement. It shall be used where shown on the
Drawings.
4.5.

Binding wire shall be 16-gauge Soft iron wire.

4.6.

Reinforcement shall be obtained only from manufacturers approved by Engineer.
Each consignment of reinforcement steel shall be accompanied by the
manufacturers certificate or shall refer to a previous certificate, if
consignment is from the same batch, showing that the reinforcement

Technical Specifications-OPAL

complies with the specified requirement. If such certificate is not made available
or if Engineer considers that the manufacturer's tests are inadequate, samples
shall be taken for acceptance test from different consignments as Engineer may
direct and shall be tested at the contractor's cost. If the result of such tests show
that the sample does not meet with the specifications the whole consignment
shall be rejected and removed from the site at the Contractor's cost.

5.

BAR BENDING SCHEDULES

5.1.

The Contractor shall prepare bar bending schedules of all the reinforcing steel bars
and these bar bending schedules shall be submitted to Engineer for his approval.
The Contractor shall obtain approval of the bar bending schedules before starting
actual bar bending works.

6.

CUlliNG, BENDING AND PLACING

6.1.

The Contractor shalt. furnish, cut bend and place all reinforcement.

6.2.

Reinforcement is to be accurately placed as shown in the drawings, and secured
against displacement by using 16-gauge G.I wire ties or suitable slips at
intersections and supported from the formwork by using concrete, or metal chairs
and spacers or hangers of an approved pattern. Where concrete blocks are used
for ensuring the cover, they shall be made of mortar not less than 1 part of cement
to 2 parts of sand. All reinforcement including dowels, remain exposed in the work
shall be suitable protected against corrosion by a thick coat of cement slurry until
embedded in concrete.

6.3.

Bars used for concrete reinforcement shall be fabricated in accordance with the
dimensions shown in the bar bending schedule approved by Engineer.

6.4.

The cutting tolerance for all bars shall be + 1 inch.

6.5.

Where an overall or an internal dimension of a bent bar is specified in the schedule,
the bending tolerance, unless otherwise stated, shall be as in Table-i..

SCOPE

The work under this section of the Specifications consists of furnishing aR plant,
labour, equipment, appliances and materials and in performing all operations in
connection with the design, supply and installation of formwork for the purpose
of shuttering in concrete work, complete in strict accordance with this section of
the specifications and the applicable drawings and subject to the terms and
conditions of the Contract.

It shall be the responsibility of the Contractor to perform the work by engaging
well trained and experienced staff or by the sub-contractor who shall have enough
number of well trained and experienced staff to coordinate these activities with
the other operations. However, the Contractor shall be responsible for the quality
of work performed by the sub-contractor as per the requirements of these
specifications.

3. DELIVERY AND STORAGE
3.1.

Delivery

The delivery of formwork materials shall be done in such a manner that dan

Technical Specifications-OPAL
3.2. Storage - Section 01600

i.

Form work should be stored, after cleaning and preparing for reuse if used
before in such a manner that access to all different materials is available.

ii.

Material which can be affected by weathering shall be stored in
appropriate building or under covers and shade.

4. WORKMANSHIP

4.1.

Forms shall have sufficient strength to withstand the pressure resulting from
placement and vibration of the concrete and shall have sufficient rigidity to
maintain specified tolerances.

4.2.

Where required, details and locations of special forms to be used are set out on
the drawings. Engineer shall refuse any work in any part of the building, which has
been constructed with a non-approved formwork. Engineer shall refuse any
concreting which will not be perfect or may not conform to the approved model.

4.3.

Earth cuts shall not be used as forms for vertical surfaces of reinforced concrete
work unless required as such or and permitted by Engineer.

4.4.

Mud centering shall not be permitted without the prior approval of Engineer.

4.5.

Formwork shaLl be of wrought timber, steel, plywood and such special materials,
as may be shown on the drawings or approved by Engineer, which give the required
finish to the surface of concrete. Wooden formwork shall be free from loose knots
and shall be well seasoned.

4.6.

The formwork shall conform to the shape, lines and dimensions as shown on the
plans, and be so constructed as to remain sufficiently rigid during the placing and
compacting of the concrete, and shall be sufficiently tight to prevent loss of liquid
from the concrete.

4.7.

The design and Engineering of the formwork, as well as its construction, shall be
the responsibility of the Contractor. Where necessary, to maintain the specified
tolerances, the formwork shall be cambered to compensate for anticipated
deflections in the formwork due to the weight and pressure of the fresh concret, and due to construction loads.

-ycU

/>"

Technical Specifications-OPAL

4.8.

The Contractor shall establish and maintain in an undisturbed condition and until.
final completion and acceptance of the project, sufficient control. points and bench
marks to be used as references for checking upon tolerances.

4.9.

Where natural plywood-form-finish, grout-cleaned-finish, smooth-rubbedfinish, scrubbed-finish, or sand-floated- finish is required, forms shall be smooth
(faced with plywood, liner sheets, or pre-fabricated panels) and true to line, in
order that the surfaces produced will require little dressing to arrive at true
surfaces. Where any as- cast finish is required, no dressing shall be permitted in
the finishing operation.

4.10. Whereas-cast surfaces, including natural plywood-form- finish are specified, the
panels of material against which concrete is cast shall be orderly in arrangement,
with joints between panels planned in approved relation to openings, building
corners, and other architectural features.
4.11. Where panels for as-cast surfaces are separated by recessed or otherwise
emphasized joints, the structural design of the forms shall provide for locating
form ties, where possible, within the joints so that patches of tie holes will not fall
within the panel areas.
4.12. Forms shall not be re-used if there is any evidence of surface wear and tear or
defect which would impair the quality of the surface finish. Forms shall be
thoroughly cleaned and properly coated before re-use.
4.13. The formwork shall be designed so that the soffits of slabs and sides of beams,
columns, and walls may be removed first, leaving the forms to the soffits of beams
and their supports in position.
4.14. Forms shall be sufficiently tight to prevent loss of mortar from the concrete.
Unless otherwise specified in the Contract Documents chamfer strips shall be
placed in the corners of forms to produce beveled edges on permanently exposed
surfaces. Interior corners on such surfaces and the edges of formed joints will not
require beveling unless required by the Contract Documents.
4.15. Positive means such as wedges or jacks for accurate adjustment and for proper
removal of shores and struts shall be provided and all settlement
monitored during concrete placing operation. Forms shall be securel bçacecl J
against lateral defl.ections.

Technical Specifications-OPAL

4.16. Where concreting of thin members is required to be carried out within formwork

of considerable depth, temporary openings in the sides of the formwork shall be
provided where necessary to facilitate the placing and consolidation of concrete.
Small temporary openings shall also be provided at the bottom of the formwork
for columns, walls and deep beams to permit the cleaning out of debris and
observation immediately before concrete is deposited.
4.17. Form ties shall be constructed so that the ends or end fasteners can be removed
without causing appreciable spatling at the faces of the concrete. After the ends
or end fasteners of form ties have been removed, the embedded portion of the ties
shall terminate not less than 2 diameter or twice the minimum dimension of the
tie from the formed faces of concrete to be permanently exposed to view and in
no case shall this distance be less than 20 mm. When the formed face of the
concrete is not to be permanently exposed to view, form ties may be cut off flush
with the formed surfaces.
4.18. Through bolts may be permitted, provided that they are greased to allow for easy
withdrawal and the holes subsequently made good. Through bolts are not to be
used on water-retaining structures.
4.19. At construction joints contact surface of the form sheathing for flush surfaces
exposed to view shall overlap the hardened concrete in the previous placement by
no less than 25 mm. The forms shall be held against the hardened concrete to
prevent offsets or loss of mortar at the construction joint so as to maintain a true
surface.
4.20. Wood forms for wall opening shall be constructed to facilitate loosening, if
necessary, to counteract swelling of the forms.
4.21. Wedges used for final adjustment of the forms prior to concrete placement shall
be fastened in position after the final check.
4.22. Formwork shall be so anchored to shores or to other supporting surfaces or
members that upward or lateral movement of any part of the formwork system
during concrete placement will not occur.
4.23. Runways or planks for moving labour and equipment shall be provided with stfttsTiL?
or legs and shall be supported directly on the formwork or upon the s '-uç{ural
member without resting on the reinforcing steel.

Technical Specifications-OPAL

4.24. All surfaces of forms and embedded materials shall be cleaned of any
accumulated mortar or grout from previous concreting and of all other foreign
material before placing fresh concrete.
4.25. Forms shall be sufficiently tight to prevent leakage of grout or cement paste.
Board forms having joints opened by shrinkage of the wood shall be removed and
replaced. Plywood and other wood surfaces not subject to shrinkage shall be
sealed against absorption of moisture from the concrete by either
i.

a field applied, approved form oil or sealer, or

ii.

a factory applied non-absorptive liner.

4.26. When forms are coated to prevent bond with concrete, it shall be done prior to
placing of the reinforcing steel. Excess coating material shall not be allowed to
stand in puddles in the forms nor allowed to come in contact with the concrete
against which fresh concrete will be placed. Care shall be taken that such approved
composition is kept out of contact with the reinforcement. Where as-cast finishes
are required, materials which will impart a stain to the concrete shall not be
applied to the form surfaces. Where the finished surface is required to be painted,
the material applied to form surfaces shall be compatible with the type of paint to
be used.
4.27. For reinforced concrete, in no circumstances shall forms be struck until the
concrete attains a strength of at least twice the stress to which the concrete may
be exposed at the time of striking.
4.28. The strength referred to shall be that of concrete using the same cement and
aggregates, with the same proportions, and cured under conditions of
temperature and moisture similar to those obtaining in the work. Where possible,
the formwork should be left for longer time as it would assist the curing.

4.29. In normal circumstances (generally where
temperatures are above 20°C and where
ordinary cement is used, forms may be struck

directed by Engine

General

such joints to the Engineer for his approval.

AppLication

3.1.

Vertical construction joints shall be formed against a stop board and horizontal
construction joints shall be formed in horizontal level.

3.2.

Except where shown otherwise on the drawings, reinforcement shall continue
through construction joints.

3.3.

Contraction joints required will be as shown on the drawings. Contraction joiflts.
shall not be hacked, wetted or mortared before concrete is placed agains,thè

3.4.

As soon as possible after the formwork has been struck for vertical jointl oti after
the concrete has set in horizontal joints, the surface [aitance of the hrie/
'<l

Technical Specifications-OPAL

concrete on the face of the joint shall, be removed to expose the coarse aggregate
in such a manner that the loosened particles of aggregate and damaged concrete
are not left on the surface. The exposed face shall be swept clean of foreign matter
and laitance.
3.5.

Feathered construction joints will not be permitted. Immediately before placing
the new concrete, neat cement grout shall be poured over the old concrete
followed for horizontal joints by a 12mm thickness of sand cement mortar of the
same materials and proportion to be used in the new concrete.

Expansion Joints
1. GeneraL

Technical Specifications-OPAL

1.1.

Expansion joints shall be provided where shown on the drawings. They shall. be
constructed with an initial gap between the adjoining parts of the works of the
width specified in the drawings. The contractor shall ensure that no debris is
allowed to enter expansion joints.

2.

References
D545 — Expansion Joint Filler
D994 — Specification for Joint Fillers for Concrete Construction

3.

AppLication

3.1.

Expansion joints shall be provided with joints filler, a joint sealing compound and
in water proof concrete water bar.

3.2.

Open joint fillers Where shown on the drawings, open joints in the structure shall
be filled with one of the following of expansion joint fillers:
i.

In internal areas a material conforming to IS:1838 containing bitumen
emulsion fibers or cork granules bound together with natural resin;

ii.

In external areas a material comprising closed cell rubber or containing cork
granules bound together with natural resin.

3.3.

The joints filler shall be easily and uniformly compressible to its original thickness,
tam parable, easily cut or sawn, robust, durable, resistant to decay due to termite
or weathering, unaffected by water and free of any constituent which will bleed
into or stain the concrete.

3.4.

The joint filler shall be of same thickness of the joint width, it shall extend through
the full thickness of the concrete unless otherwise specified and shall be
sufficiently rigid during handling and placing to permit the formation of straight
joints.

7.

CRACKS

7.1.

If any cracks develop in the reinforced cement concrete construction which in the
opinion of the Engineer may be detrimental to the strength of the construction,
the contractor at his own expense shall test the structural element in question. If
under these test loads the cracks shall develop further the contractor at his own
expense shall dismantle the construction, cart away the debris, replace the
construction and carryout all consequential work there to at no extra cost. If the
cracks are not detrimental to the stability of the construction in the opinion of the
Engineer the contractor at his own expense shall grout the cracks with
pneumatically applied mortar or epoxy grout or by other specified treatment as
directed by the Engineer at his own expense and risk he shall also made good al
other building work such as plaster, moulding, surface finish of floors, roofs, ceiling
etc. which in the opinion of the Engineer have suffered damage either in
appearance or stability owing to such cracks.

7.2.

The repair work shall be carried out to the satisfaction of the Engineer. The
decision of the Engineer as to the extent of the liability of the contractor in the
above matter shall be final and binding on the contractor.

8.

LOAD TESTING ON COMPLETED STRUCTURES

8.1.

During the period of construction or within the defect liability period the Engin
may at his discretion order the load testing of any completed structure or any

I

Technical Specifications-OPAL

thereof if he has reasonable doubts about the adequacy of the strength of such
structure for any the following reasons:
i.

Results of compressive strength on concrete test cyUnders.

ii.

Premature removal of formwork.

iii.

Inadequate curing of concrete.

iv.

Over loading during the construction of the structure or part
thereof.

v.

Carrying out concreting of any portion without prior approval of
the Engineer.

vi.

Honey combed or damaged concrete which in the opinion of the
Engineer is particularly weak and will affect the stability of the
structure to carry the design load, more so in important or critical
areas of the structure.

vii.

Any other circumstances attributable to alleged negligence of the
contractor which in the opinion of the Engineer result in the
structure or any part thereof being of less than the expected
strength.

8.2.

All the loading tests shall be carried out by the contractor strictly in accordance
with the instructions of the Engineer. Such tests should be carried out only after
expiry of minimum 28 days or such longer period as directed by the Engineer.

8.3.

The structure should be subjected to a super imposed load equal to 1.25 times the
specified superimposed load assumed in the design. This load shall be maintained
for a period of 24 hours before removal. During the test, struts strong enough to
take the whole Load shall be placed in position leaving a gap under the members
as directed.

8.4.

The deflection due to the superimposed load shall be recorded by sufficient
number of approved deflect meters capable of reading up to 1/500 of a cm and
located suitably under the structure as directed by the Engineer.

8.5.

If within 24 hours of the removal of the superimposed load, the structures do not
recover at least 75% of the deflection under the superimposed load, tpetest-.
loading shall be repeated after a lapse of 72 hours. If the recovery after t

-

test is less than 80% of the maximum deflection shown during the second

Technical Specifications-OPAL

structure shall be considered to have failed to pass the test and shall be deemed
to be unacceptable.
8.6.

In such cases the part of the work concerned shall be taken down or cut out and
reconstructed to comply with the specifications. Other remedial. measures may be
taken to make the structure secure at the discretion of the Engineer. Moreover,
such remedial measures shall be carried out to the complete satisfaction of the
Engineer. (vi) All costs involved in carrying out the tests and other incidental
expense thereto shall be borne by the contractor regardless of the result of the
tests. The Contractor shall take down or cut out and reconstruct the defective
work or shall make the remedial measures instructed at his own cost. (vii) In
addition to the above load tests, nondestructive test methods such as core test
and ultrasonic pulse velocity test shall be carried out by the Contractor at his own
expense if so desired by the Engineer. Such tests shall be carried out by an agency
approved by the Engineer and shall be done under expert's guidance using only
recommended testing equipment.

9.

DEFECTIVE CONCRETE WORK

9.1.

If the results of load test or core test on any concrete structure found
unsatisfactory or unacceptable, the concrete work and the structure shall be
removed and redone by the contractor at his own risk and coast as instructed by
Engineer.

The contractor's supervisor who are in-charge of concreting work shall be skilled
in this class of work and shall personally superintend all the concreting operations.

3.

Contractor 's WORK AND STORAGE AREA

3.1.

The Contractor shall make its own arrangements for any necessary off-site
storage or shop areas necessary for the proper execution of the WORI<.

3.2.

Should the Contractor find it necessary to use any additional land for its camp or
for other purposes during the construction of the WORI<, it shall provide for the
use of such lands at its own expense.

3.3.

The Contractor shall construct and use a separate storage area for hazardous
materials used in constructing the WORK.

3.4.

For the purpose of this paragraph, hazardous materials to be stored in the
separate area are all products labeled with any of the following terms: Warning,
Caution, Poisonous, Toxic, Flammable, Corrosive, Reactive, or Explosive.

3.5.

In addition, whether or not so labeled, the following materials shall be stored in
the separate area: diesel fuel, gasoline, new and used motor oil, hydraulic f'uid,
cement, paints, and paint thinners, two-part epoxy coatings, sealants, asphaltic
products, glues, solvents, wood preservatives, sand blast materials, and spill
absorbent.

3.6.

The Contractor shall develop and submit to the Engineer a plan for storing and
disposing of the materials above.

3.7.

The separate storage area shall meet all the requirements of all authorities having
jurisdiction over the storage of hazardous materials.

3.8.

The separate storage area shall be inspected by the Engineer prior to construction
of the area, upon completion of construction of the area, and upon clean-up and
removal of the area.

3.9.

All hazardous materials which are delivered in containers shall be stored in the
original containers until use. Hazardous materials which are delivered in bulk shall
be stored in containers which meet the requirements of authorities having
jurisdiction.

3.

MateriaL

3.1.

All the Material that is required for the Execution of this Activity shall be Proviçied-----by the Client that shall conform to ASTM C652.

/ /.%:

Material under this Activity once provided to the Contractor shall, shall shift all

Technical Specifications-OPAL

3.3.

Contractor shall Arrange all the storage Facilities for such at its own cost that shall
be open to inspection for the Client and Engineer at all times.

3.4.

The Contractor shall store the material at clean, undamped area, safe from all
debris and Weather Conditions.

4.

Application
4.1. Soaking of Blocks
4.1.1. Blocks shall be soaked in water for a minimum period of one hour before use.
When Blocks are soaked, they shall be removed from the tank sufficiently in
advance so that at the time of laying they are skin dry. Such soaked blocks
shall be stacked on a clean place where they are not spoilt by dirt, earth, etc.

5.

Laying Blocks

5.1.

The blocks shall be built in English bond with upwards facing blocks work (for
chimney made and fair faced machine-made bricks both).

5.2.

The Block Masonry shall conform to ASTM C90 Specifications.

5.3.

The Blocks Shall be of 3 Sizes as defined Below.

5.4.

•

4"

•

6"

•

8"

Each block shall be set with bed and vertical joints filled thoroughly with mortar.
Selected blocks shall be used for the exposed blockwork as specified under [1. The
walls shall be taken up truly plumb. All courses shall be laid truly horizontal and
vertical joints shall be truly vertical.

5.5.

Vertical joints in alternate course shall come directly over the other. The thickness
of blocks courses shall be kept uniform and for this purpose wooden straight edge
with graduation giving thickness of each block course including joint shall be used.

5.6.

Necessary tools comprising of wooden straight edge, mason's sprit level, square,
foot rule, plumb, line and pins etc. shall be frequently and fully used by the msóri...to ensure that the walls are taken up true to plumb, line and levels.

Technical Specifications-OPAL

5.7.

Both the faces of walls of thickness greater than [•] cm shall be kept in proper
plane. All the connected blockwork shall be carried up nearly at one level and no
partition of work shall be raised more than one meter above the rest of the work.
Any dislodged block shall be removed and reset in fresh mortar.

5.8.

Before commencing any blockwork, the Contractor shall confer with other trades
to ensure that all pipes, conduits, drains, sleeves, bolts, hangers, or any other
materials necessary to be installed in the blockwork at the time it is built, have
been fixed or provided for.

6.

Joints

6.1.

Blocks shall be laid that all joints are full of mortar. The thickness of joints shall be
not more than 20 mm. The face joints shall be raked to a minimum depth of 10mm
by a raking tool during the progress of the work when the mortar is still green, so
as to provide proper key for the plaster or pointing to be done.

6.2.

Where plastering pointing is not to be done, the joints shall be struck flush and
finished at the time of laying. The face of brickwork shall be kept cleaned and
mortar dropping removed.

6.3.

Jointing with Existing Structures

6.4.

When fresh masonry is to be placed against existing surface of structures, the
surface shall be cleaned of all loose materials, roughened and wetted as directed
by the Engineer so as to affect a good bond with the new work.

7.

Openings

7.1.

Openings in bt.ockwork for air conditioning ducts, exhaust fans, grills pipes etc.
shall be provided at the time of laying blockwork without any extra cost.

7.2.

After installation of piping, conduits, grills, etc. all openings left around pipes,
conduits, grills etc. shall be checked and caulked with cement mortar to render the
whole work vermin proof and tidily finished.

7.3.

The rates quoted are deemed to be inclusive of closing such pre-deterrnlned
openings including erection and dismantling of scaffolding if required, the/ptaing
of inserts, collars, grills etc. to be paid separately under respective items. \\ '

Technical Specifications-OPAL

8.

Curing

8.1.

Green work shall, be protected from rain by suitable covering. Masonry work in
cement mortar shall be kept constantly moist on all faces for a minimum period
of seven days. The top of the masonry work shall be left flooded with water so as
not to disturb or washout the green mortar.

8.2.

During hot weather, all finished or partly completed work shalt be covered or
wetted in such a manner as to prevent rapid drying of the block work.

9.

ScaffoLding

9.1.

The scaffolding shall be sound and strong to withstand all loads likely to come
upon it. The holes which provide resting space for horizontal members shalt not be
left in masonry under one meter in width or immediately near the skew backs of
arches. The holes left in the masonry work for supporting the scaffolding shall be
filled and made good.

10.

Condition of Equipment

10.1. All equipment used for mixing or transporting mortar and blocks shall be clean
and free from set mortar, dirt or other injurious foreign substances.

11.

WaLLing Building:

11.1.

Blocks shall be wetted before being laid and the top of walling where left off shalt
be wetted before re-commencing building. Walls to be kept wet three days after
building.

11.2.

Blocks shall be welt buttered with mortar before being laid and the brickwork
carried up evenly course so that no part is allowed to be carried up more than 90cm
higher at any time than any other part.

12.

Setting out WaLling

12.1. The contractor shall provide proper setting- out rods and set out all work ônit'for
corners, openings, heights, etc. And shall build the watts and piers etc. To theidth,

depth and height indicated on the drawings and as directed and approved by the
Engineer in-charge.

Construction Surveying
1.

DESCRIPTION

1.1.

The WORK under this Section includes providing all labor, materials, tools and
equipment necessary to perform all surveying and staking necessary for the
completion of the Project in conformance with the Drawings and Specifications
and standard engineering and surveying practices, including all calculations
required to accomplish the WORK.

2.

CONSTRUCTION

2.1.

All surveying involving property lines shall be done by, or under the direction of
Engineer or its Representative, or any Qualified as per the satisfaction of the
Engineer.

2.2.

The Client will supply information relative to the approximate locations of and
corners, but final responsibility for locations, referencing, and restoration shall
rest with the Contractor.

2.3.

In the event the Contractor does not replace the survey and property corners
disturbed by the Contractor 's operations, the Client may, after first notifying the
Contractor, replace with its own responsibility. The cost of such replacementsshatt
be deducted from payments to the Contractor.

Technical Specifications-OPAL

2.4.

The Contractor shall provide the Client with a copy of all surveyors notes, if
requested by the Engineer, prior to each Pay Request payment for which payment,
Construction Surveying, is increased from the previous Pay Request payment.

2.5.

The Contractor shall provide the Client with a copy of ati surveyors' notes, prior to
the request for final payment, and include the information on the record drawings.

2.6.

The Contractor shall obtain alt information necessary for as-built plan production,
from actual measurements and observations made by its own personnel, including
Subcontractors, and submit this information to the Engineer.

2.7.

The Contractor shall use competent, qualified personnel and suitable equipment
for the layout work required and shall furnish alt stakes, templates, straightedges
and other devices necessary for establishing, checking and maintaining the
required points, lines and grades.

2.8.

The Contractor shall perform all staking necessary to delineate clearing and/or
grubbing limits; all cross sections necessary for determination of excavation and
embankment quantities, including intermediate and/or remeasure cross sections
as may be required; all slope staking; all staking of culverts and drainage
structures, including the necessary checking to establish the proper location and
grade to best fit the conditions on site; the setting of such finishing stakes as may
be required; the staking of right-of-way; the staking, referencing and other
actions as may be required to preserve or restore land and property corners; and
all other staking necessary to complete the project.

2.9.

Field notes shall be kept in standard bound notebooks in a clear, orderly and neat
manner, consistent with standard engineering and surveying practices. The
Contractor's field books shall be available for inspection by the Engineer at any
time.

2.10. All field survey notes, including those which become source documentations from
which quantities for payment are computed, shall be recorded by a note keeper
furnished by the Contractor. The note keeper shall be thoroughly familiar with
generally accepted standards of good survey note keeping practice.

I

Shading concrete work.
ii.

Ponding method.

SLJBMITTALS

2.1.

DELIVERY, STORAGE, AND HANDLING

3.1.

Deliver curing materials in manufacturer's original packaging including applicbe-instructions and manufacturer's safety data sheets (MSDS).

I \\

I

Technical Specifications-OPAL

4.

MATERIALS

4.1.

The Hessian Cloth sheet shall be securely be lined/laid on the surface with proper
Sprinkling of Water.

4.2.

The polyethylene shall be securely bonded to the burlap so that there will be no
separation.

4.3.

Liquid Membrane-Forming Compounds for Curing Concrete: Liquid membrane
forming compounds for curing concrete shall and conform to ASTM C309, Type 10 with a red or white fugitive dye. Use a white dye unless otherwise directed by
Engineer.

4.4.

Polyethylene Film: Polyethylene film shall conform to ASTM D2103. The film shall
have a thickness of six (6) mils and be a white opaque color.

4.5.

Evaporative Retardant: Confirm ASTM Standards or approved equal.

4.6.

Water: Only water from sources approved by Engineer shall be used.

5.

AppLication

5.1.

Perform the WORK in accordance with this SPECIFICATION and in accordance with
applicable ACI standards. When a conflict occurs between this SPECIFICATION and
ACI, the ACI standard shall control. All materials shall be used in accordance with
the manufacturer's printed instructions, a copy of which shall be on site.

5.2.

Beginning immediately after placement, concrete shall be protected from
premature drying, excessively hot or cold temperatures, and mechanical injury,
and shall be maintained with minimal moisture loss at a relatively constant
temperature for the period necessary for hydration of the cement and hardening
of the concrete in accordance with ACI 308.1.

5.3.

The materials and method of curing shall be subject to review and acceptance by
Engineer. Specific curing requirements may be called out on the DRAWINGS.

5.4.

Curing shall be continued for at least seven (7) days. Alternatively, if tests are made
of cylinders kept adjacent to the structure and cured by the same methods,
moisture retention measures may be terminated when the average compressive
strength has reached seventy percent (70%) of the specified concrete strength ( /
r::

/

I

Technical Specifications-OPAL
6.

CURING METHODALOGY

6.1.

Perform curing of concrete by curing compound, by moist curing, by moisture
retaining cover curing, or combinations thereof, as herein specified.

6.2.

Provide moisture cu ring by one of the following methods:

6.3.

Keep concrete surface continuously wet by covering with water.

6.4.

Use continuous water-fog spray.

6.5.

Cover concrete surface with moisture retaining cover specified in

6.6.

Place cover to provide coverage of concrete surfaces and edges with four- (4-)
inch lap over adjacent moisture retaining covers, and seal using waterproof tape
or adhesive. Immediately repair any holes or tears during curing period using cover
material and waterproof tape.

6.7.

Provide liquid membrane curing compound specified in Article Materials to
concrete surfaces as follows:

6.8.

Apply specified curing compound to concrete slabs within one (1) hour of final
finishing operations or within one (1) hour of form removal. Apply uniformly in
continuous operation by spray or roller in accordance with manufacturer's
directions and these SPECIFICATIONS.

6.9.

Recoat areas subjected to heavy rainfall within three (3) hours after initial
application. Maintain continuity of coating and repair damage during curing
period.

6.10. Liquid Membrane Forming Compound and Evaporative Retardant
Applicators/Sprayers: Membrane curing and evaporative retardant compounds
shall be applied with a sprayer capable of maintaining a constant pressure.
Spraying membrane curing compounds or evaporative retardants by other
methods, such as rolling, shall be approved by Engineer.
6.11. When a spray-applied membrane-curing compound is used, it shall be applied in
two (2) coats with the second coat applied at right angles to the first coat.
6.12. If finish materials are to be applied to the surface of concrete, follow
manufacturer's recommendations to remove membrane curing compound.

7.

PROTECTION

a
Technical Specifications-OPAL

7.1.

During the curing period, the concrete shall be protected from damaging
mechanical disturbances, such as load stresses, heavy shock, and excessive
vibration. All finished concrete surfaces shall be protected from damage by
construction equipment, materials, or methods, by application of curing
procedures, and by rain or running water. Self-supporting structures shall, not be
loaded in such a way as to overstress the concrete.
